name: PN-943
class: Oral alpha-4 beta-7 integrin antagonist peptide
route: Taken by mouth twice a day in trials
status: Not FDA-approved. A phase 2 ulcerative colitis trial reported in 2022; no phase 3 trial is registered
mechanism: Blocks the alpha-4 beta-7 integrin on gut-homing immune cells so fewer enter the intestinal lining, acting mainly inside the gut

article.summary: PN-943 is an experimental oral peptide that blocks the alpha-4 beta-7 integrin to keep immune cells out of the inflamed gut. A phase 2 ulcerative colitis trial showed a modest signal, and it is not approved.
article.takeaway: PN-943 is an experimental peptide taken by mouth that aims to do inside the gut what the infused antibody vedolizumab does: block alpha-4 beta-7 integrin, a surface protein that helps immune cells enter the intestinal wall in inflammatory bowel disease. In the phase 2 IDEAL study of about 160 adults with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis, 27.5% on the 150 mg twice-daily dose reached clinical remission at 12 weeks versus 14.5% on placebo, a difference that was not statistically significant (P=0.08), and the higher dose did not separate from placebo.[^1] No phase 3 trial is registered, and PN-943 is not approved.
glance: Investigational; not approved by the FDA
By mouth, twice daily in the phase 2 trial
Oral, gut-restricted alpha-4 beta-7 integrin antagonist peptide
One phase 2 trial (IDEAL) and a healthy-volunteer study; no phase 3 registered

blocks.text: In ulcerative colitis, immune cells travel from the blood into the lining of the large intestine and drive inflammation. The alpha-4 beta-7 integrin acts like a docking key that lets some of those cells enter the gut. Blocking it is a proven approach: vedolizumab, an antibody given by infusion or injection, works this way.

PN-943 is a small peptide designed to bind the same integrin but to stay mostly in the gut after swallowing, which could limit exposure elsewhere in the body. A study in healthy volunteers measured its blood levels and effects after single and multiple oral doses.[^2]

Protagonist Therapeutics ran the phase 2 IDEAL trial, which the registry lists as completed in 2023.[^3] The company said in 2022 that the 150 mg dose would advance toward a phase 3 program and that it was seeking a partner to help fund it.[^4] As of late 2026, no PN-943 phase 3 trial is listed on ClinicalTrials.gov.

blocks.text: The overall difference missed the usual threshold for statistical significance, and the subgroup result needs confirmation in a larger trial. The company also reported histologic and endoscopic improvement on the lower dose.[^1]

items: **IDEAL:** the rate of adverse events on the 150 mg dose was similar to placebo, according to the company.[^1]
**Design goal:** staying mostly in the gut was intended to limit exposure elsewhere in the body.[^2]
**Unknown:** long-term safety has not been tested in larger or longer trials.

blocks.text: Without a registered phase 3 trial, PN-943's future is uncertain. Any benefit would need to be confirmed in a larger study that meets its main endpoint in the overall population, not only in a subgroup.

evidence.label: Early: one phase 2 trial that missed its main test
evidence.text: Human evidence is one phase 2 trial and a healthy-volunteer study.[^1][^2] The lower dose looked promising, but the main comparison was not statistically significant, and the results appeared in company announcements and news reports rather than a full journal article.

faq.q: How is PN-943 different from vedolizumab?
faq.a: Both block the alpha-4 beta-7 integrin. Vedolizumab is an antibody given by infusion or injection, while PN-943 is a small peptide taken by mouth and designed to act mainly in the gut.[^1][^2]

faq.q: Did PN-943 work in ulcerative colitis?
faq.a: The lower dose showed a higher remission rate than placebo (27.5% vs 14.5%), but the difference was not statistically significant, and the higher dose did not separate from placebo.[^1]
No. It is investigational, and no phase 3 trial is registered.[^3]
